items.title: The Extraordinary Art of Tudor Embroidery
items.description:
Embroidery was a staple at the Tudor Court. It decorated the huge halls of palaces like Hampton Court, and adorned the clothes of Kings, Queens, and aristocrats. The Bacton Altar Cloth is an incredible surviving example of the embroidery techniques used by Elizabethan embroiderers, which may have once been part of a dress worn by Elizabeth I.

global_silver_linings.title: Longest Predator Exclusion Fence in the Pacific Protects Thousands of Ground-Nesting Seabirds
global_silver_linings.snippet: In 2022, the longest “predator exclusion fence” anywhere in the Pacific was completed on Kauai, encircling 168 acres of prime seabird nesting habitat. The nesting birds include endangered species that were under constant threat of ravaging feral cats and pig before the 11,200-foot-long fence was raised. Now, 4 years later, these seabirds are following their […] The post Longest Predator Exclusion Fence in the Pacific Protects Thousands of Ground-Nesting Seabirds appeared first on Good News Network .
global_silver_linings.reason: A landmark predator exclusion fence is giving thousands of ground-nesting seabirds a genuine fighting chance to breed and thrive in safety — proof that determined conservation engineering can turn the tide for vulnerable wildlife. When we build walls to protect rather than divide, nature responds with remarkable resilience.

discovery_articles.title: Denby Dale Railway Viaduct in Denby Dale, England
discovery_articles.snippet: This impressive 21 arch viaduct is on a railway line currently called the "Penistone Line" and originally built in  by the  Huddersfield and Sheffield Junction Railway (later to become part of the Lancashire & Yorkshire Railway ). The valley of the River Dearne was a major barrier to the line between Huddersfield, West Yorkshire, England and the town of Penistone (NW of Sheffield) to join up with the Manchester, Sheffield and Lincolnsire Railway and so provide a shorter route to London via the North Midland Railway. The viaduct is 112 feet above the valley at its highest and the arches have a span of 40 feet.

discovery_articles.snippet: Off the coast of Philadelphia (or more accurately, Camden County, New Jersey), sitting in the Delaware river and heavily covered in trees and brush, is a deserted island. Once home to CITGO industrial operations, the island has been overgrown and uninhabited by human life for years. Usually, it’s off limits to visitors, but thanks to the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection and the Center for Aquatic Sciences, a conservation easement allows the occasional group of visitors for educational purposes.

featured_read.title: The Grasshopper and the “Lusory Attitude” Essential for Playing the Game of Life
featured_read.snippet: On a recent flight, I watched a mother across the aisle play peek-a-boo with her small son while next to me a grown man in a VR headset spent six hours ascending the levels of a video game. It occurred to me that what I was doing between them — reading — was also a game: a peek-a-boo of ideas advancing across levels of meaning. I thought of Newton, who reflected on his deathbed: “I don’t know what I may seem to the world, but, as to myself, I seem to have been only like a boy playing on the… read article
featured_read.blurb: This essay traces a philosopher's quietly radical argument that play isn't what we do when life pauses — it's the very posture that makes life worth living. At its heart is one luminous question: what if the willingness to accept a game's arbitrary rules is the same muscle we use to accept being mortal?
